summary: Web of Worlds is a Metaverse Standards Forum direction for making virtual worlds addressable and linkable with ordinary web machinery, announced by the Forum's 3D Web Interoperability Working Group on 2 June 2026. Its whole normative surface is three small OpenAPI files at version 0.0.1 — a world API, an asset API and a user manifest API — plus a README table of five core requirements saying a world is joined, followed, previewed, saved and shared by its URL. It is strong on one idea, that a world is a URL and its parts hang off that URL, and it does that well. Almost everything else a working group would look for is absent rather than wrong: no units, no scale, no up axis, no bounds, no coordinate reference system, no signature, no destination on a portal, and no way for one world to contain another. The first trap is that none of the three files uses a single normative keyword and no schema requires a single property, so an empty object validates as a World, a User, a Node, a Portal, a View and a Spatial descriptor alike; a team that reads the whitepaper will expect decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials, selective disclosure, glTF, USD and X3D, and will find none of them in the machine-readable text. The second trap is now demonstrated rather than predicted: the world README puts the scene graph under /wow/scene/, the machine-readable file puts it under /wow/spatial/{spatialID}, and the project's own reference implementation, simpleWorlds, publishes a third OpenAPI file that serves /wow/scene/node/{nodeId}. The specification and its reference implementation disagree about the normative graph path, so two good-faith servers cannot talk.

coverage.note: The core of the subject: a world is a URL, joined, followed and previewed by URL fragment, and its parts hang off that same URL as URL/wow/world and URL/wow/user/4182. The whitepaper states the idea directly and the world README turns it into the five core requirements.

sources.title: WoWAPI OpenSpatialWorld API (commit d39a1a0)
sources.quote: The main purpose is to join, connect and share the spatial world.

coverage.note: The world API can read a world's status, including live aspects, as a standardised container such as JSON-LD, and a world is saved by bookmarking its URL. There is no whole-world import, though the API can create and update individual scene nodes, so the two directions are uneven: world status comes out whole, while only single nodes go in. There is also no whole-world file that carries assets and behaviour and no statement of what survives if the host closes; the specification is at draft version 0.0.1.
